1) Top / card index — Show {카드 등급} and {카드 문양} symbol at the top-left and mirrored bottom-right corners, in a clean playing-card layout.
2) Hero area — Place the subject from {참고 이미지} centered, emerging from the flat illustrated card with realistic depth and strong perspective.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]

Premium Korean hair salon portfolio ad, clean, trustworthy, and transformation-focused.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render these strings verbatim in the image: {메인 제목}, {시술명}, {비포 라벨}, {애프터 라벨}, {시술 태그 1}, {시술 태그 2}, {시술 태그 3}, {가격 라벨}, {가격}, {예약 문구}, {날짜}.

Create a warm cafe dessert review photo with handwritten Korean annotations.
Transform an ordinary table shot into a cozy SNS-style cafe diary image with realistic cafe-table details, date/location labels, and playful review stickers.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Use {참고 이미지} as the base composition and preserve the real food/table perspective.
- Main focus: {대표 디저트} placed lower center or center-left, with {보조 디저트} slightly behind it.
- Include {음료 구성} around the edges as supporting objects, cropped naturally with condensation, cup sleeves, straws, lids, or ceramic reflections where appropriate.
- Background treatment: warm cafe table, soft bokeh, dappled sunlight, realistic plates, forks, napkin folds, a small receipt corner, and subtle crumbs or cream smears that fit an actual dessert review scene.
- Keep handwritten annotations integrated into the photographed table surface, following perspective and lighting.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Top label area — add a small diary sticker containing "{날짜 라벨}" and "{위치 라벨}" near the upper-left cafe-table area; place {좌측 메모} nearby, slightly tilted, with a small sun doodle and underline.
2) SNS identity strip — add "{인스타 핸들}" in a small handwritten tag near the top or cup area, with tiny save/share-style micro icons and a heart count label "{좋아요 라벨}".
3) Hero area — keep {대표 디저트} sharp and appetizing; draw a white dotted outline following its silhouette and add a small rating badge "{평점 라벨}" beside the plate.
4) Mid section — keep {보조 디저트} visible behind the hero dessert; add white dotted outline, sparkle doodles, and a tiny flavor tag "{맛 태그}".
5) Bottom / side notes — place {디저트 메모} near the hero dessert and {우측 메모} near the upper-right dessert area; add curved arrows, hearts, small stars, and a short hashtag strip "{해시태그}" in {낙서 스타일}.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: casual Korean handwritten marker, rounded strokes, slightly uneven baseline, like writing over a printed cafe photo.
- Color palette: warm cream #F7E8D0, dessert brown #4A2A1A, matcha green #6B7C3D, strawberry red #D8423A, ink white #FFF8EF, pale sticker beige #F2D9B6.
- Use thin white doodle lines, 2-4 px visual weight, semi-transparent but readable; labels may use cream paper tape shapes with soft shadows.
- Keep tableware realistic; preserve shadows, reflections, crumbs, cream texture, cake pores, strawberry seeds, ice, condensation, and paper/ceramic material details.
- If cups, sleeves, receipts, or packaging are visible, keep them naturally integrated and photographically plausible; do not flatten them into graphic blocks.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm lifestyle food photography, close table angle, shallow depth of field.
- Lighting: late afternoon sunlight from upper-left, leaf-shadow patterns, soft warm highlights.
- Color grade: cozy golden brown, slightly muted contrast, film-like cafe diary tone.
- Finishing: realistic SNS review-photo overlay, soft sticker shadows, hand-drawn doodles that sit on the image without turning the food into an illustration.

[6. MOOD]
Cozy Korean cafe diary, sweet dessert review, warm and playful, like a saved Instagram cafe recommendation post from a sunny afternoon.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render these strings verbatim in the image: "{좌측 메모}", "{디저트 메모}", "{우측 메모}", "{날짜 라벨}", "{위치 라벨}", "{인스타 핸들}", "{좋아요 라벨}", "{평점 라벨}", "{맛 태그}", "{해시태그}".
- Keep handwritten Korean fully legible with no broken characters, especially small labels and hashtag text.
- Food anatomy must remain realistic: correct cake slice geometry, natural strawberry shape, believable cream thickness, no melted plastic look.
- Dotted outlines must follow dessert edges cleanly without covering key textures.
- Do not alter the reference photo into an illustration; keep it photographic.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications.
- Broken Korean characters.
- Celebrity composites or implying a real celebrity endorsement.
- Fake government, school, medical, or award-style authority marks.

[1. PURPOSE]
Create a premium restaurant brand campaign contact sheet with exactly 8 distinct food group-shot images.
Each panel shows a different realistic dining-table composition while keeping one elegant brand tone for {브랜드명} and the same featured menu lineup.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall layout: polished 4x2 grid, exactly 8 separate rectangular image panels, thin dark gutters, no extra panels.
- Each panel features the same menu lineup: {메뉴 1}, {메뉴 2}, {메뉴 3}, {사이드 메뉴}, {음료}.
- Use {테이블 소재} and {배경 스타일} consistently, with varied camera distance, crop, spacing, plate orientation, hand-off-frame serving cues, steam, sauce sheen, garnish details, and tableware placement.
- Include realistic premium restaurant details: ceramic plates, black bowls, lacquer tray, brass or stainless cutlery, chopsticks, spoons, folded linen napkins, small dipping sauce dishes, seasonal garnish, condensation on {음료}, subtle crumbs or sauce traces where natural, and a small printed menu card.
- Keep the brand tone for {브랜드명} refined, structured, appetizing, warm, and editorial.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Top row panel 1 — overhead flat lay: all five items arranged around a small neutral menu card printed with “{브랜드명}”, “셰프 추천”, “{음식 카테고리} 테이스팅”, and tiny item names “{메뉴 1} · {메뉴 2} · {메뉴 3} · {사이드 메뉴} · {음료}”.
2) Top row panel 2 — 45-degree hero angle: {메뉴 1} slightly forward, {메뉴 2} and {메뉴 3} staggered behind, {사이드 메뉴} in a small bowl, {음료} with visible condensation, chopsticks resting diagonally on a linen napkin.
3) Top row panel 3 — close cropped diagonal layout: strong diagonal flow across plates, glossy sauce highlights, garnish texture, shallow background falloff, a small table tent showing “오늘의 추천” and “{브랜드명}”.
4) Top row panel 4 — wide table spread: generous restaurant-table scene with all five items, sauce dishes, folded napkin, water glass, menu booklet corner, and warm ambient background from {배경 스타일}.
5) Bottom row panel 5 — centered symmetric set: balanced plating with {메뉴 1}, {메뉴 2}, {메뉴 3} in premium plates, {사이드 메뉴} centered below, {음료} above, small gold-accent menu strip labeled “{브랜드명}”.
6) Bottom row panel 6 — asymmetrical editorial table arrangement: dishes placed naturally off-center with textured linen, dipping sauce, garnish leaves, spoon, chopsticks, and a small receipt-style reservation card reading “디너 코스” and “{브랜드명}”.
7) Bottom row panel 7 — intimate close-up with background blur: {메뉴 1} and {메뉴 2} sharply detailed in foreground, {메뉴 3}, {사이드 메뉴}, and {음료} still clearly present in background, visible steam, glossy sauce, crisp edges, and ceramic texture.
8) Bottom row panel 8 — low-angle table-level hero shot: dramatic restaurant perspective with all five items visible in layered depth, {음료} catching rim light, premium tableware silhouettes, warm highlights, and a small menu card bearing “{브랜드명}”.
9) Food placement — every panel includes one clear serving of each featured menu item; vary dish order, plate height, garnish direction, cup position, and prop placement in every panel.
10) Props — use black bowls, elegant plates, chopsticks, spoons, cups, bottles, napkins, sauce dishes, menu cards, and small restaurant service details in a tasteful premium way.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: no oversized advertising headline; use refined Korean sans or serif microtype only on menu cards, reservation slips, table tents, or small brand labels.
- Korean text rendered in the image may include: “{브랜드명}”, “셰프 추천”, “오늘의 추천”, “디너 코스”, “{음식 카테고리} 테이스팅”, “{메뉴 1}”, “{메뉴 2}”, “{메뉴 3}”, “{사이드 메뉴}”, “{음료}”.
- Palette: black stone, deep red, warm ivory highlights, dark charcoal shadows, subtle gold accents.
- Border / shadow: thin dark gutters between panels, soft dish shadows, premium editorial spacing, realistic table contact shadows, natural reflections on ceramic and glass.
- Food realism: appetizing textures, moist surfaces, crisp garnish, accurate portion scale, believable steam, sauce thickness, and correct perspective for bowls, plates, cups, chopsticks, and spoons.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: realistic commercial food photography, mix of 35mm overhead, 50mm editorial, 85mm shallow depth, and 100mm food close-up across panels.
- Lighting: soft directional studio lighting from upper-left, controlled highlights on sauces and tableware, gentle background falloff, rim light on glassware, warm bounce on ivory plates.
- Color grade: high-end restaurant campaign, rich contrast, appetizing warm highlights, polished blacks, refined deep red background, natural food color fidelity.
- Material detail: emphasize {테이블 소재} grain or surface finish, ceramic glaze, matte black bowls, linen fibers, brass or stainless utensil reflections, condensation droplets on {음료}, and subtle sauce gloss.

[6. MOOD]
Premium restaurant campaign, refined dining experience, elegant editorial food spread, appetizing warmth, crafted plating, and sophisticated hospitality.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: if text appears, it must be one of these exact strings only: “{브랜드명}”, “셰프 추천”, “오늘의 추천”, “디너 코스”, “{음식 카테고리} 테이스팅”, “{메뉴 1}”, “{메뉴 2}”, “{메뉴 3}”, “{사이드 메뉴}”, “{음료}”.
- Generate exactly 8 panels, not 7, not 9, not a single merged table scene.
- All 8 panels must have clearly different camera angle, crop, menu arrangement, spacing, plate orientation, and prop placement.
- Every panel must clearly include {메뉴 1}, {메뉴 2}, {메뉴 3}, {사이드 메뉴}, and {음료}.
- Food must look realistic, fresh, premium, and edible; tableware must be geometrically correct.

studio:prompts3:ours-1214.content:
[INPUT]
- reference_image: {참고 이미지}
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Cinematic AR-style music card portrait poster with a central subject and layered floating album cards, designed like a premium social wallpaper, digital promo cover, and realistic music editorial portrait.
Vertical portrait format with strong depth separation, neon-accented frosted glass UI cards, readable Korean micro-copy, realistic studio atmosphere, and a content-rich music showcase feel.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- {참고 이미지}를 기준으로 {주제 인물}을 정확히 중앙 정렬하고, 얼굴과 상반신이 가장 먼저 보이도록 55~60% 프레임 비중으로 배치합니다.
- 배경은 {배경}의 어두운 스튜디오 톤을 유지하되, 가장자리로 갈수록 더 짙게 떨어지는 비네팅, 실제 촬영 같은 보케 점광원, 얇은 안개 입자, 후면 LED 라이트 반사를 넣어 깊이감을 만듭니다.
- 인물 전면과 후면에 {카드 수}장의 {카드 스타일} 음악 카드를 오비트처럼 분산 배치하되, 카드가 얼굴과 눈을 가리지 않도록 시선 라인을 명확히 확보합니다.
- 카드 간 간격은 균등하지 않게 설정해 원근감을 주고, 전경 카드 2~3장은 어깨 주변에 살짝 걸치게, 나머지는 배경 깊이로 후퇴시키며 일부는 측면으로 기울어진 3D 유리 패널처럼 보이게 합니다.
- 포스터 상단에는 작은 에디토리얼 라벨과 날짜를 넣습니다: “AR MUSIC PORTRAIT”, “VOL.1214”, “2026.05 ISSUE”.
- 하단에는 작은 크레딧 라인과 핸들 텍스트를 넣습니다: “MODEL CREDIT  {주제 인물}”, “@night.playlist”, “SELECTED TRACKS / PERSONAL MIX”.
- 우측 하단에는 실제 잡지/프로모션 커버처럼 얇은 바코드형 그래픽, 작은 QR-like 코드 블록, 제작 크레딧을 배치하되 공식 인증처럼 보이지 않게 디자인합니다.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Hero portrait layer: {참고 이미지} 기반의 {주제 인물}을 선명하게 유지하고, 피부 결, 머리카락 가장자리, 얼굴 윤곽, 의상 질감이 실제 스튜디오 포트레이트처럼 또렷하게 보이도록 중앙에 배치합니다.
2) Foreground cards: 어깨와 가슴 앞쪽에 반투명 카드 2~3장을 겹치고, 유리 표면에는 얇은 지문 같은 미세 반사, 가장자리 빛 번짐, 살짝 흐릿한 후면 굴절을 넣어 인물보다 앞에 떠 있는 느낌을 줍니다.
3) Mid-depth cards: 나머지 음악 카드를 인물 좌우와 후면에 원호 형태로 배치하고, 카드의 회전각과 크기를 조금씩 달리해 3D 오비트 구성을 만듭니다. 각 카드의 깊이 차이가 보이도록 그림자, 블러, 하이라이트 방향을 달리합니다.
4) Card content: 각 카드에는 {노래 목록}의 곡명을 한 장당 하나씩 균등 분배하여 산세리프 제목 텍스트로 넣습니다. 카드마다 트랙 번호 “TRACK 01”, “TRACK 02”, 러닝타임 “03:42”, 작은 파형 그래픽, 앨범 썸네일 느낌의 추상 컬러 블록, 짧은 한국어 태그를 추가합니다.
5) Korean micro-copy: 카드와 포스터 곳곳에 짧고 자연스러운 한국어 문구를 넣습니다: “오늘의 무드”, “야간 드라이브”, “차가운 공기”, “반복 재생”, “나만의 믹스”, “새벽 플레이리스트”.
6) Background atmosphere: {배경} 위에 미세한 입자감, 소프트 보케, 얕은 빛 번짐, 어두운 스튜디오 벽의 은은한 질감, 바닥 또는 후면에 반사되는 네온 라이트를 추가해 실제 촬영과 디지털 인터페이스가 섞인 분위기를 만듭니다.
7) Depth and focus: 인물과 중간면 카드는 가장 선명하게, 전경 카드는 카메라에 가까운 유리처럼 약간 소프트하게, 후경 카드는 강한 블러와 낮은 대비로 처리해 레이어 분리를 명확히 합니다.
8) Edge glow treatment: 카드 테두리, 일부 UI 라인, 머리카락 림라이트, 어깨 주변 윤곽선에 {색상 팔레트}의 틸/보라 네온 글로우를 얇게 입혀 음악 앱 AR 인터페이스처럼 강조합니다.
9) Final polish: 전체 대비를 높이되 피부 톤은 자연스럽게 유지하고, 카드 표면의 프로스트 글래스 질감은 반투명하고 고급스럽게 조절합니다. 인물, 카드, 텍스트, 배경의 빛 방향이 서로 일관되게 연결되도록 마무리합니다.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: clean sans-serif like Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, medium to semibold weight, card title size 24~34px, small UI labels 12~14px, tracking slightly expanded. Main track titles should be crisp and legible; micro labels may be smaller but still plausible.
- Korean title treatment: use short Korean labels as editorial accents, for example “오늘의 무드”, “새벽 플레이리스트”, “반복 재생”. Keep them clean, modern, and accurately rendered.
- Color palette: cool teal / violet neon, charcoal black, muted silver, neutral skin tone; accent hex colors such as #55FFE2, #8A5CFF, #10131A, #D7DCE6, with {색상 팔레트} influencing glow, UI lines, and bokeh reflections.
- Border/shadow: frosted glass card with rounded corners, 1.5px neon edge, soft outer glow 8px blur at 18% opacity, subtle drop shadow 0px 12px 28px at 22% opacity, plus faint inner highlight along the top-left card edge.
- Surface texture: semi-transparent matte glass with slight blur diffusion, realistic refraction, soft fingerprints, subtle dust sparkle in the light, no heavy chrome, no plastic shine.
- Graphic details: include small waveform strips, track number labels, tiny equalizer bars, album-art color tiles, date label, handle, volume/issue text, barcode-like promo block, and tiny production credits to make the portrait feel like a finished digital cover.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Sony A7R IV, 85mm f/1.8, ISO 200, 1/250s, portrait framing with shallow depth of field. If {카메라/렌즈} provides a specific setup, preserve that look while keeping the same premium 85mm portrait feel.
- Lighting: {조명}; softbox key light from camera-left at 45°, weak rim light from camera-right, subtle fill from front to preserve skin texture, controlled specular highlights on glass edges, and teal/violet practical LED reflections on the cards.
- Color grade: cool neon editorial grade with deep navy shadows, teal highlights, violet edge accents, restrained skin warmth, subtle halation around bright edges, and realistic shadow roll-off.
- Render quality: high-resolution editorial realism, natural skin texture, realistic hair detail, believable optical blur, layered glass refraction, and crisp typography where intended.

[6. MOOD]
Premium futuristic music-editorial poster — somewhere between a high-end streaming canvas concept, a night-city portrait session, and a Kinfolk-meets-cyberpunk digital cover. The image should feel personal, atmospheric, and collectible rather than sterile: a real portrait surrounded by floating music memories.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: "입력 이미지 — 본인 X 사진", "20대 한국인 남성 상반신 정면, 뉴트럴 표정, 스트리트 캐주얼", "Tuscan Leather", "Hotline Bling", "4422", "Hold On, We're Going Home", "Best I Ever Had", "Nice For What", "What Did I Miss"
- Additional Korean text rendered in image should be short and accurate: "오늘의 무드", "새벽 플레이리스트", "야간 드라이브", "반복 재생", "나만의 믹스", "차가운 공기".
- Keep the subject identity consistent with the reference image.
- Do not cover the subject's eyes with any card, glow, or UI element.
- Distribute the song titles across the cards so each card shows one track name clearly.
- Keep all floating cards readable enough to feel intentional, while preserving the portrait as the main focus.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals or certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Unauthorized celebrity composites or misleading celebrity likeness

studio:prompts3:ours-1213.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean meme-style cinematic still of three business chairmen teasing a younger Korean man about not buying stocks.
Designed as a viral reaction-image frame with realistic faces, expressive gestures, and a lively chicken-and-beer restaurant setting full of believable table details, readable Korean meme text, and social-media-ready humor.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: The three chairmen occupy the upper-middle 55% of the frame in a tight conversational cluster, leaning toward the 30대 남성, while the younger man sits lower-right as the punchline and visual reaction target.
- Background treatment: Casual Korean chicken restaurant interior with dark wood booths, warm beige walls, stainless beer mugs, fried chicken plates, wall menu strips, small beer posters, a call bell, receipts, wet tissue packs, sauce dishes, and a realistically busy-but-clean tabletop.
- Spacing and framing: Tight mobile-readable meme framing with all faces turned inward toward the young man; foreground table items and background signage add depth, context, and humor without hiding the expressions.
- Meme overlay: Add one bold top caption in Korean and one smaller bottom reaction caption, integrated like a premium viral reaction image rather than a flat graphic.
- Use {주제_장면}, {인물_묘사}, {장소_분위기}, {조명_톤}, {구도_앵글}, {카메라_렌즈}, {비율} placeholders naturally throughout the render instruction.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero area (upper 60%): 삼성 이재용 회장, 엔비디아 젠슨 황 회장, SK 최태원 회장이 서로 다른 표정으로 30대 남성을 향해 장난스럽게 훈계하듯 말하는 순간을 포착, 각 인물의 얼굴 디테일과 손짓이 선명하게 보이게 배치. 이재용은 차분한 미소로 손가락을 살짝 들어 말하고, 젠슨 황은 검은 가죽 재킷 차림으로 맥주잔 옆에서 웃으며 농담하고, 최태원은 고개를 살짝 기울인 채 “왜 안 샀어?” 같은 표정으로 바라본다.
2. Interaction area (center-right): 30대 남성은 살짝 긴 머리와 스트릿 패션 차림으로, 어깨가 살짝 움츠러든 채 민망하고 억울한 표정으로 시선을 피하는 리액션을 연기. 그의 앞 스마트폰 화면에는 작은 주식 차트 앱처럼 보이는 초록·빨강 캔들 그래프가 희미하게 보이고, 옆에는 구겨진 영수증과 냅킨 위 낙서처럼 “그때 살걸”이 적혀 있다.
3. Table area (lower third): 바삭한 프라이드 치킨 한 접시, 양념 소스, 치킨무, 종이컵, 생맥주잔의 거품, 맥주 피처, 치킨 뼈, 젖은 휴지 포장, 콜벨, 계산서 트레이를 자연스럽게 배치. 테이블 위 작은 메뉴 카드에 “후라이드 19,000”, “양념치킨 21,000”, “생맥주 500cc 4,500”, “오늘의 안주”가 읽히게 넣는다.
4. Background area (full frame edges): 한국식 치킨집 내부가 따뜻한 보케로 살아 있고, 벽면에는 “치맥은 타이밍”, “주문은 벨을 눌러주세요”, “VOL.247 오늘의 회식” 같은 작은 장식 문구와 맥주 포스터, 메뉴판, 계산대 조명이 보인다. 배경 손님 실루엣은 흐릿하게 두어 현장감만 주고, 주인공들의 표정과 손짓이 가장 먼저 읽히게 한다.
5. Caption layer: Top meme caption set in bold Korean: “주식 안 산 30대의 최후”. Bottom reaction caption set smaller: “형님들… 치킨은 제가 살게요”. Add a tiny lower-left social watermark-style handle: “@stock_chimaek_meme” and a small date label: “2026.05.01 금요일 밤”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Pretendard Bold 700 for the main meme caption and Pretendard Medium 500 for smaller labels, compact and mobile-readable, with clean Korean letterforms, tight line spacing, subtle black stroke or soft shadow for legibility over the warm restaurant background.
- Color palette: warm amber #C98A3A, deep brown #4A2E1F, creamy beige #F3E7D3, chicken-gold #D9A441, beer-foam white #F7F4EE, muted charcoal #2B2B2B, plus small stock-chart accents in red and green.
- Border/shadow: soft realistic drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity; subtle table-edge shadow and natural occlusion shadows under plates, glasses, hands, and receipts to separate characters and objects from the background.
- Detail density: Add believable restaurant micro-details such as condensation on beer glasses, crispy chicken texture, oil sheen on sauce, wood grain on the table, paper receipt fibers, menu-card lamination reflections, and warm reflections on stainless mugs.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Sony A7R V with 85mm f/1.4 GM, ISO 400, shot at f/1.8 for shallow depth of field and crisp facial texture.
- Lighting: warm indoor practical lights mixed with a soft key light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from front-right, and a subtle rim light separating hair and shoulders from the background.
- Color grade: warm editorial grade with amber highlights, natural skin tones, slightly muted shadows, and mild cinematic contrast.
- Realism: High-resolution cinematic realism with believable skin texture, natural eye highlights, authentic restaurant reflections, and editorial meme polish; the scene should feel like a captured moment from a premium Korean sitcom mixed with a finance meme.

[6. MOOD]
Light-hearted Korean comedy still with a premium business-parody energy, like a news meme frame blended with a high-end sitcom reaction shot. The humor should come from timing, awkward eye contact, and the contrast between serious business figures and casual 치맥 banter.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: Render all visible Korean text exactly and clearly with no broken characters: “주식 안 산 30대의 최후”, “형님들… 치킨은 제가 살게요”, “후라이드 19,000”, “양념치킨 21,000”, “생맥주 500cc 4,500”, “오늘의 안주”, “치맥은 타이밍”, “주문은 벨을 눌러주세요”, “그때 살걸”, “2026.05.01 금요일 밤”.
- Anatomy/layout invariants: All four faces must remain anatomically realistic, with natural hand poses and exactly 5 fingers per hand; the three chairmen must read as distinct individuals, and the young man must remain the obvious reaction target.
- Joke tone: Render the scene as playful teasing and friendly banter, with no physical intimidation; expressions should be amused, surprised, embarrassed, or mock-serious rather than hostile.
- Placeholder fidelity: Preserve the meaning of {주제_장면}, {인물_묘사}, {장소_분위기}, {조명_톤}, {구도_앵글}, {카메라_렌즈}, {비율} exactly when applying the scene.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-1212.content:
[INPUT]
- reference_image: {참고 이미지}
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
YouTube thumbnail for creator-facing content, reaction videos, variety-show commentary, drama/vlog edits, and high-click short-form topic packaging.
A horizontal thumbnail composition combining a personal photo, oversized Korean headline text, a punchy accent shape/emoji, creator handle, and a small view-bait label for immediate mobile readability.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- {참고 이미지} occupies the left 60-65% of the frame, with the face and upper torso emphasized so the expression reads instantly at small thumbnail size.
- Use the right 35-40% as a high-impact typography block for {헤드라인}, with {강조 문구} and {채널 핸들} integrated like a real creator thumbnail package.
- Apply {배경 처리} across the canvas: slightly darkened original background, cinematic contrast, subtle vignette, and a soft glow/rim-light around the subject for separation.
- Crop the subject in a tight, punchy composition that feels like a dramatic reaction thumbnail, while keeping enough space for the headline and accent graphics.
- Add one bold accent shape near the headline, such as a diagonal burst, rounded sticker, underline slash, or speech-bubble tab, using {악센트 컬러} and {액센트 이모지} as a click-driving visual cue.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Main Image Area (left 60-65%):
   - {참고 이미지} is preserved with natural proportions, keeping the original facial expression, pose, eye direction, and framing energy intact.
   - If the source image has a detailed background, keep recognizable atmosphere but darken and blur it gently so the face remains the visual anchor.
   - Add subtle edge separation around the subject, like a thin soft glow or rim highlight, to create a professional Korean entertainment thumbnail feel.
   - Preserve realistic skin texture and lighting while enhancing clarity around the eyes, mouth, and silhouette.
2. Headline Zone (right side / {글자 위치}):
   - Place {헤드라인} in very large bold Korean sans-serif lettering, aligned to {글자 위치} and stacked in 1-3 short lines if needed.
   - Fill text with {글자 컬러}; add a thick black outline, inner highlight, and drop shadow so the wording stays crisp on mobile screens.
   - Set the headline to {글자 크기}, dominating the right side without covering the subject’s face.
   - If {서브 텍스트} is provided, place it in a smaller pill label above or below the headline, in white or pale gray with a dark translucent backing.
3. View-Bait & Channel Details:
   - Add {강조 문구} as a compact sticker-style label, for example in the top-right or above the headline, using {악센트 컬러} with black or white text.
   - Add {채널 핸들} in small but readable type near the lower-right corner or along a small vertical tab, like an authentic creator branding mark.
   - Add {액센트 이모지} once near the headline or emphasis label, sized large enough to be noticed but secondary to {헤드라인}.
   - Add {장식 태그} as one or two small hashtag-style or topic-chip captions near the bottom edge, supporting the video topic without overpowering the main text.
4. Background & Readability Layer:
   - Apply a mild vignette, controlled background blur, and tonal compression behind the text zone to increase separation.
   - Keep the composition energetic with diagonal shapes, glow strokes, subtle halftone dots, or speed-line accents appropriate to Korean variety and creator thumbnails.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold, Noto Sans KR Black, Gmarket Sans Bold, or a similar heavy Korean sans-serif; headline should feel like a classic Korean variety thumbnail font with extreme mobile readability.
- Color palette: {글자 컬러}, deep black #000000 for outline and shadow, {악센트 컬러} for burst/sticker details, subdued charcoal gray #1A1A1A for background compression, with neutral skin tones preserved.
- Border/shadow: black outline 6-10px thickness, soft shadow with 4px vertical offset, 12-18px blur, 25-35% opacity for separation and legibility.
- Accent graphics: use one bold sticker, speech bubble, underline slash, or burst shape; make it look designed and intentional, not like random clutter.
- Layout: optimized for 1536x1024 horizontal canvas, with the main readable action kept inside a central thumbnail-safe crop area for platform previews.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: treat the source as a sharp editorial still, comparable to an 85mm portrait look or a close-crop 50mm frame depending on the input image.
- Lighting: preserve the original lighting of {참고 이미지}; if enhancement is needed, emulate a soft studio key from upper-left with gentle fill from front-right so the face stays bright against the darkened background.
- Color grade: {톤·결}, with slightly cool shadows, neutral skin tones, crisp facial detail, and high-contrast text treatment against a subdued dark backdrop.
- Post-processing: selective sharpening on eyes and headline, subtle glow around accent graphics, and a gentle cinematic vignette toward the corners.

[6. MOOD]
K-드라마 reaction thumbnail meets Korean variety-show clickbait energy: dramatic, expressive, polished, and instantly readable like a creator thumbnail for entertainment commentary, dating talk, vlog confession, or reaction content.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: "{헤드라인}" must appear exactly as written, with every Hangul character clean, complete, and readable at small thumbnail size.
- If used, "{서브 텍스트}", "{강조 문구}", "{채널 핸들}", and "{장식 태그}" must be spelled exactly as provided.
- Rendered Korean thumbnail text example hierarchy: main headline "{헤드라인}" largest, sticker label "{강조 문구}" second, handle "{채널 핸들}" small, tag "{장식 태그}" smallest.
- Preserve the subject’s expression and overall composition from {참고 이미지}; do not change facial emotion, eye direction, or body pose.
- Headline must remain the dominant visual element with thick outline, strong contrast, and immediate mobile readability.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals, government marks, certification stamps, or misleading verified badges
- Broken Korean characters, misspelled Hangul, garbled glyphs, or unreadable text
- Altering the subject’s facial expression, identity, or eye direction
- Celebrity face composites or implying a real celebrity endorsement unless explicitly provided in the reference image

args.default: K-드라마 / 예능 / 브이로그 감성의 약간 시네마틱한 썸네일 톤, 클릭을 유도하는 강한 대비

studio:prompts3:ours-1211.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Create a portrait-oriented vintage newspaper front page featuring a personal or authorized selfie as the main lead story image.
Designed to feel like a real archival daily newspaper cover with date, edition marks, article columns, captions, section labels, and press-era typography, suitable for social sharing and print-style editorial parody.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: Center {원본 인물} as the hero photo occupying 55-60% of the vertical frame, with the face aligned near the visual center and the torso cropped chest-up for a strong front-page anchor.
- Background treatment: Build the page on distressed newsprint paper in off-white and warm gray, with visible fiber grain, faint halftone dots, slight ink bleed, registration softness, fold marks, and subtle aging stains.
- Spacing and framing: Use a full newspaper 1면 hierarchy: masthead and issue metadata across the top, narrow weather/price/date line, a framed portrait block in the middle, side teasers, caption strip, and dense article columns at the bottom with page number and section markers.
- Editorial realism: Add realistic print details such as column rules, small boxed notices, photo caption typography, byline text, edition label, barcode/price box, tiny printer marks, and slightly uneven ink density.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header area (top 15%): Set {신문 제목} centered in a bold vintage masthead treatment, using wide letter spacing, black ink on paper tone #F4F0E6, with thin horizontal separator rules above and below the title. Add a top metadata line reading "2026년 5월 1일 금요일 · 제247호 · 서울판 · 값 1,500원" plus small left/right utility text blocks such as "오늘의 인물" and "아카이브 특별판".
2. Main image area (mid 60%): Insert {원본 인물} as the feature photograph, cropped shoulders-up or chest-up, preserving natural facial proportions and expression, with a printed-photo border, halftone overlay, and subtle ink bleed to match newspaper reproduction. Beneath the photo, add a readable caption strip: "사진 제공: 본인 · 기록된 순간, 오늘의 1면이 되다".
3. Surrounding editorial elements: Add compact side teasers around the portrait without covering the face, such as "단독 인터뷰", "라이프 섹션 A3", and "오늘의 한마디". Include a small barcode/price area in a lower corner and tiny vertical printer text near the gutter: "PRINTED IN SEOUL · ARCHIVE EDITION".
4. Footer area (bottom 25%): Place {헤드라인} as the dominant headline block, then add 3-4 newspaper article columns with readable Korean body snippets, bylines, pull quotes, small rule lines, and subheads. Example subheads: "나다운 순간을 기록하다", "새로운 하루의 첫 장면", "독자들이 주목한 표정". Include page label "1면" and section marker "A".
5. Overall layout integration: Apply {구도} as the fixed page hierarchy so the masthead, portrait, headline, article columns, captions, and issue details read instantly as a classic front-page newspaper composition. Apply {지면 톤} consistently to determine how aged, formal, dramatic, or warm the printed page feels.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Pretendard Bold or Noto Sans KR Bold for {신문 제목} and {헤드라인}; masthead should feel like a condensed display serif or slab-serif newspaper logo, while the headline should be large, heavy, and tightly set like a front-page lead. Body copy should use smaller newspaper-style Korean serif/sans text with varied weights for byline, caption, and article columns.
- Color palette: Restrict the page to black #111111, ivory #F4F0E6, warm gray #B8B0A6, charcoal #2B2B2B, and light sepia #D9CBB8; keep all accents muted and print-like.
- Border/shadow: Add a faint printed-edge frame around the portrait, subtle paper crease texture across the page, and a soft drop shadow with 2px y-offset, 8px blur, and 10% opacity to separate the hero image from the newsprint background.
- Newspaper texture: Use real press details: halftone grain on the portrait, slightly rough ink edges on large type, column dividers, fold crease down the page, ink offset marks, and minor corner wear.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Simulate a classic 85mm portrait lens at f/2.8 with a medium-format editorial feel, crisp facial focus, and gentle edge falloff similar to a scanned magazine portrait.
- Lighting: Use soft studio light from upper-left at roughly 45° with low-contrast fill from front-right, avoiding harsh specular highlights and preserving a clean printed-photo look.
- Color grade: Black-and-white base with a slight sepia wash, lifted paper whites, restrained midtone contrast, and archival press reproduction tonality.
- Print finish: Make the final image look like a physically printed newspaper page photographed or scanned flat, with tactile paper fibers, authentic black ink saturation, and subtle tonal variations across the sheet.

[6. MOOD]
Classic front-page editorial — like a museum archive newspaper reproduction with a polished magazine-cover sensibility, newsroom authenticity, and the charm of a personally featured headline story.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: The rendered artwork must show these strings exactly: "{신문 제목}", "{헤드라인}", "2026년 5월 1일 금요일", "제247호", "서울판", "값 1,500원", "오늘의 인물", "아카이브 특별판", "사진 제공: 본인", "기록된 순간, 오늘의 1면이 되다", "단독 인터뷰", "라이프 섹션 A3", "오늘의 한마디", "나다운 순간을 기록하다", "새로운 하루의 첫 장면", "독자들이 주목한 표정", "1면", "섹션 A". Render Korean without broken characters, spacing errors, or missing glyphs.
- Anatomy/layout invariants: Preserve the subject's facial identity, expression, and proportions; no facial distortion, no extra limbs, and keep the masthead / portrait / headline / article-column page hierarchy intact.
- Layout realism: The page must read as a complete newspaper front page, with date and edition information, article columns, captions, page markers, and fold/section details integrated around the hero portrait.

- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Create a polished pixel art avatar sprite sheet for one specific person, presented as a realistic indie-game character production asset with eight consistent poses and useful design annotations.
Designed for indie game UI, character select screens, profile/avatar asset packs, portfolio pages, and game-dev documentation.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: Place each sprite centered inside its grid cell, with identical scale, head size, and body proportions across all 8 poses.
- Background treatment: Use {배경} as the sheet base, enhanced with a subtle pixel-grid or transparent-checker production surface, small coordinate ticks, and soft cell dividers so it feels like a real game asset sheet.
- Spacing, framing direction: Keep even gutters between cells and enough safe area so hair, hands, props held by the character, clothing details, and feet remain fully visible.
- Production-sheet framing: Add a compact header bar, asset metadata strip, palette swatches, and small Korean pose labels to make the image content-rich while keeping the sprites dominant.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Grid layout (main frame): Build a {레이아웃} that fills the canvas with consistent cell spacing, visible frame boxes, tiny row/column markers, and a professional sprite-export feel.
2. Character fidelity: Convert {원본 인물} into simplified pixel art while preserving recognizable facial silhouette, hairstyle, eyewear if present, skin tone, clothing color blocking, and memorable personal details.
3. Pose set rendering: Show {포즈 세트} as distinct expressions and actions, with each pose clearly readable at thumbnail size and matching the same character design.
4. Pixel specification: Render the sprites at {픽셀 크기} with crisp hard-edged pixels, intentional stair-step curves, readable facial pixels, and consistent sprite proportions.
5. Sprite consistency: Keep line thickness, pixel density, palette usage, facial identity, and silhouette scale identical across all panels so the sheet feels like one cohesive production asset.
6. Sheet details: Include a top title area reading “본인 픽셀 아바타 시트”, a small version/date label such as “v1.0 · 2026.05”, an asset ID like “PLAYER_01”, compact pose labels such as “대기”, “걷기”, “인사”, “점프”, and a side palette column with labeled color chips for skin, hair, outfit, shadow, and accent colors.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use crisp pixel-font typography for Korean labels and metadata. Keep text small but legible, aligned to the grid, and rendered as intentional pixel lettering rather than smooth vector type.
- Color palette: Use a compact palette based on the source image, with clean separations between skin, hair, clothing, and background; favor classic game colors such as #F7F7F7, #D9D9D9, #8C8C8C, #2B2B2B, plus the original image’s dominant accent colors.
- Border/shadow: Use thin one-pixel cell borders, tiny corner registration marks, and subtle internal pixel edge contrast around each sprite. Add small interface-like details such as frame numbers, tile-size notes, and palette chips without overpowering the character.
- Detail density: Add believable production annotations, micro UI marks, color swatches, and frame labels that would naturally exist on a game sprite sheet.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: N/A for digital pixel art; emulate a front-facing sprite capture and game-asset presentation rather than a photographed scene.
- Lighting: Flat, evenly distributed digital lighting with pixel-art shadow clusters inside the character design where needed for readability; no photographic depth blur.
- Color grade: Crisp retro game palette with restrained saturation, clean contrast, and a modern indie-game documentation look.
- Rendering finish: Sharp nearest-neighbor pixel edges, no anti-aliased blur, visible pixel structure, and a carefully arranged production-board layout suitable for export previews.

[6. MOOD]
Polished indie-game character asset sheet — classic Game Boy Advance / SNES sprite production feel with modern portfolio-ready presentation, playful UI metadata, and a believable game-dev workflow atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: if Korean text appears, render it exactly and legibly, especially “본인 픽셀 아바타 시트”, “대기”, “걷기”, “인사”, “점프”, “표정”, “완료”.
- Ensure all 8 sprites depict the same individual with identical facial identity, hairstyle, and clothing design.
- Each panel must use the same layout, scale, and alignment so the character reads as one consistent sprite set.
- Preserve the requested {포즈 세트}, {배경}, {픽셀 크기}, and {레이아웃} while enriching the surrounding sheet with realistic production details.
- Use only images of the individual with permission.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals/certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likenesses

[4. STYLE RULES]

- Color palette: #FFDDC1 peach, #8C5A3C warm brown, #F5EEDC cream, #D9A066 sand, #6B4E3D dark cocoa.

- Material detail: Emphasize real camping textures such as canvas tent fabric, brushed metal lantern, wool blanket, wood grain tabletop, enamel mug highlights, dust on boots, and soft earth under the chair.

- Use a studio background in {배경색} with subtle paper grain, gentle tonal gradient, and realistic editorial print texture so the cover feels physically published rather than like a blank mockup.
- Keep the portrait vertically balanced and slightly larger than a typical interview cover to emphasize personal branding and direct eye contact.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header area (top 10–14%): Render "{잡지명}" in large bold uppercase typography centered at the very top, with tight kerning and clean baseline alignment. Add small surrounding magazine metadata: "VOL.247", "2026년 5월호", "SEOUL INTERVIEW ISSUE", and "₩7,500".
2. Hero area (mid 65–70%): Place {원본 인물} in a centered half-body pose, with sharp facial detail, natural expression, realistic skin texture, and strong separation from the {배경색} background; the face should be the visual anchor.
3. Cover-line area (left and right mid-frame): Add short editorial blurbs in Korean, set in compact stacked typography: "나다운 선택", "조용한 확신", "하루를 바꾸는 태도". Use small separator dots, thin rules, or tiny section labels like "LIFE", "WORK", "VOICE" for magazine authenticity.
4. Lower text area (bottom 15%): Set "{메인 문구}" centered below the portrait as the main cover statement, with a smaller supporting line below it such as "긴 인터뷰로 만난 오늘의 생각".
5. Bottom print details: Place a realistic barcode area, tiny publisher line "OURS MEDIA", page/issue microtext, and production credit "EDITOR 김서연 · PHOTO 이준호" near the bottom edge.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Pretendard ExtraBold for "{잡지명}" at a large cover size, Noto Sans KR Medium for "{메인 문구}", and Noto Sans KR Regular / Bold for issue labels, blurbs, barcode captions, and credit microtext. Keep all Korean lettering crisp, aligned, and high-contrast.
- Color palette: Base color {배경색}, with black #111111 for the masthead and main quote text, warm gray #6F6A63 for secondary text, and natural warm skin tones with restrained neutral highlights for the portrait.
- Editorial hierarchy: Make "{잡지명}" the biggest typographic element, {원본 인물} the visual center, "{메인 문구}" the main quote, and all feature blurbs smaller but readable like a real magazine cover.
- Print realism: Add subtle paper texture, faint ink density variation, fine halftone-like softness in flat color areas, and gentle shadowing where text overlays the portrait/background.
- Decorative details: Use thin divider lines, tiny dots, barcode stripes, side spine text, issue numbering, and small credit labels to enrich the cover while keeping the interview portrait premium.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 with an 85mm f/1.2 portrait lens, shallow depth of field, crisp focus on the eyes, and natural facial texture retained.
- Lighting: {촬영 톤} plus soft window light from the upper-left at roughly 45°, gentle fill from the right, and smooth highlight rolloff across the face.
- Color grade: Neutral editorial grade with clean whites, natural skin tones, slightly muted contrast, and refined saturation for a high-end magazine look.
- Material feel: Simulate a finished print cover photographed or rendered straight-on, with barely visible paper grain, clean ink edges, realistic tonal depth, and polished magazine production quality.

[6. MOOD]
Kinfolk and Interview magazine cover hybrid — refined Korean editorial portrait with confident personal-brand energy, real monthly-magazine metadata, concise cover lines, and a polished contemporary publishing feel.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: "{잡지명}" and "{메인 문구}" must appear exactly as written, with no broken Korean characters, spacing errors, or altered wording.
- Fixed Korean cover details must be legible and correctly spelled: "VOL.247", "2026년 5월호", "나다운 선택", "조용한 확신", "하루를 바꾸는 태도", "긴 인터뷰로 만난 오늘의 생각".
- The image must feature only the individual from {원본 인물} or a permitted subject; no additional people, reflections, duplicated faces, or split portraits.
- The face must be clear, recognizable, and centered enough for interview-cover presentation.
- "{메인 문구}" must remain short and succinct, matching a real magazine cover line.
- Portrait anatomy must be natural and realistic, with correctly rendered hands only if visible.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness mixing

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: {원본 인물} is the hero subject, centered and scaled to occupy about 60% of the frame, with a polished gold trophy held at chest-to-face height and slightly angled toward camera.
- Background treatment: Build a deep stage-like backdrop using {배경}, with layered black velvet texture, gold light streaks, warm bokeh glints, faint audience-silhouette depth, and a subtle ceremonial frame around the edges.
- Spacing and framing: Use a polished award-card layout with a top title band, central portrait stage, lower certificate panel, small profile-stat blocks, date stamp, badge icons, and footer caption arranged for instant mobile readability.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero area (mid 60%): {원본 인물} cleanly cut out and centered, realistic skin texture preserved, holding a polished gold trophy with convincing reflections, formal award-pose posture, no crop cuts on the face or hands.
2. Header text area (top 10%): Display {카드 제목} in large bold centered type near the top, with wide tracking, clean edges, and a polished event-poster headline feel. Add small supporting cover-style text around it: "AWARD", "WINNER", "NO. 1206", and "2026.05.01".
3. Label area (below header, 8%): Show {상 이름} as a smaller refined line directly under the title, center aligned, framed by thin gold divider lines and tiny laurel accents.
4. Profile and badge layer: Add realistic award-card micro details around the portrait, such as a small name-credit label "MODEL CREDIT: {원본 인물}", badge chips reading "올해의 주인공", "성취 지수 98", "응원 점수 100", and a small date-location stamp "서울 스테이지 · 2026".
5. Footer text area (bottom 12%): Place {하단 문구} centered above the lower edge with comfortable line spacing and strong contrast against the dark background. Include the exact celebratory caption "오늘의 주인공은 바로 당신입니다" as a secondary line if it is not already part of {하단 문구}.
6. Decorative ceremony layer: Add gold frame accents, certificate-style corner ornaments, subtle embossed lines, spark-like highlights, confetti flecks, velvet stage texture, and a restrained spotlight halo behind the head and trophy to reinforce the award-stage atmosphere while keeping the portrait dominant.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Pretendard ExtraBold for {카드 제목} at headline scale, Noto Sans KR Medium for {상 이름} at smaller subtitle scale, and Nanum Myeongjo SemiBold Italic for {하단 문구} at medium footer scale. Use compact Noto Sans KR Regular for micro labels, stats, date stamp, and badge text.
- Color palette: Deep black #000000, rich gold #D4AF37, bright gold #FFD700, warm metallic highlight #F6E7B5, soft charcoal #1A1A1A.
- Border/shadow: Apply a soft drop shadow around the subject and trophy (3px y-offset, 10px blur, 20% opacity), plus a thin gold frame line with a faint inner glow, embossed certificate corners, and subtle metallic reflections on all gold accents.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Phase One IQ4 with 110mm lens at f/5.6, studio portrait sharpness, crisp subject separation, premium event-photography realism.
- Lighting: Soft directional key light from upper-left at about 45°, gentle rim light from right, subtle back glow behind the head and trophy, controlled specular highlights on the trophy, and faint warm stage spill on the lower card panel.
- Color grade: Black-and-gold ceremony grade with warm metallic highlights, slightly deepened shadows, glossy trophy contrast, refined skin tones, and a mild vignette to focus attention on the center.

[6. MOOD]
High-end award ceremony editorial — feels like an Oscars red-carpet tribute card blended with a premium personal achievement certificate, polished prestige, and staged celebration energy.

[7. CRITICAL]

- Additional visible Korean microcopy may include: "올해의 주인공", "성취 지수 98", "응원 점수 100", "서울 스테이지 · 2026", "축하합니다".

[1. PURPOSE]
Create a personalized block-toy character portrait from a real-person reference as a collectible miniature figure display.
Designed for a playful gift image, profile-art concept, or boutique-style toy product render that feels photographed as a premium custom toy release.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: Center the {토이 스타일} character vertically and horizontally, with the full body and {베이스} occupying about 55–65% of the frame height; frame it like a real collectible product portrait with enough surrounding display context for labels, props, and packaging details.
- Background treatment: Use {배경} as a believable boutique toy-display backdrop, such as a soft studio sweep, collector shelf, acrylic display case, or printed backing card, with subtle depth, material texture, and realistic contact shadows.
- Spacing, framing direction: Arrange {소품} naturally around the base as curated collector accessories, with some items closer to the camera and some slightly behind the stand for depth; maintain a mostly straight-on product framing with a polished catalog feel.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero area (center): Convert {원본 인물} into a {토이 스타일} character with the same overall hairstyle silhouette, skin tone impression, outfit color family, and recognizable facial expression simplified into block-toy proportions. The figure stands upright on the {베이스} with a stable centered pose, glossy-to-matte plastic surfaces, softened bevels, molded seams, and realistic toy manufacturing details.
2. Collector display layer: Add a premium toy-display presentation around the figure, including a small clear acrylic riser or transparent dust-cover edge, a printed backing card behind the character, and subtle retail-display lighting reflections that make the figure feel physically present.
3. Prop ring (lower mid): Arrange {소품} around the feet and base like collectible accessories included with the toy. Each prop should have crisp molded detail, small highlights, realistic scale, and gentle shadows, while still supporting the main character silhouette.
4. Base treatment (bottom 15%): Render the {베이스} as a neat display stand with bevels, matte finish, tiny molded feet, and a front nameplate. Include a small printed serial detail such as “NO.1205” and a short Korean nameplate line: “나만의 블록 캐릭터”.
5. Product information details: Add realistic boutique-toy micro graphics around the display: a small barcode area, tiny edition text “CUSTOM EDITION”, date label “2026.05”, and compact Korean caption stickers such as “오늘의 주인공” and “소장용 미니 피규어”. Keep these details legible but secondary to the figure.
6. Background field (full frame): Fill the frame with {배경} enriched by soft paper grain, subtle acrylic reflections, shelf shadows, or printed card gradients. The background should feel like a real photographed toy package/display setup rather than an empty digital mockup.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use small, clean product-label typography as part of the collectible display. Render Korean text accurately: “나만의 블록 캐릭터”, “오늘의 주인공”, “소장용 미니 피규어”. Add tiny English product details such as “CUSTOM EDITION”, “NO.1205”, and “2026.05”.
- Color palette: Preserve the reference-driven color family from {원본 인물}, supported by neutral studio whites (#FFFFFF, #F7F7F5), soft gray shadows (#D9DDE3), and toy-like accent colors that match the props. Add subtle packaging-card accents and warm specular highlights only where they enhance realism.
- Border/shadow: Apply realistic grounded shadows beneath the figure, props, acrylic elements, and base; keep plastic edges crisp but slightly rounded to reinforce the toy aesthetic. Add fine contact shadows, tiny reflections, and molded-surface highlights for a tangible product-photo feel.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Studio product-shot perspective using a 50mm lens at f/8, eye-level framing, crisp focus across the full figure and accessories.
- Lighting: Even diffused studio lighting from the front-left at 45°, with a gentle fill from the right to reduce harsh contrast. Add small glossy highlights on plastic and acrylic surfaces, plus soft shadows that reveal the figure’s scale and placement.
- Color grade: Bright neutral studio grade with clean whites, soft cool grays, lightly saturated toy colors, and subtle realistic contrast; keep the product premium, cheerful, and tactile.

[6. MOOD]
Whimsical boutique collectible display — a polished designer-toy showcase with the realistic feel of a photographed custom figure, playful gift-shop packaging, and charming personal keepsake energy.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: Render all Korean text cleanly and correctly: “나만의 블록 캐릭터”, “오늘의 주인공”, “소장용 미니 피규어”. Do not garble, fragment, mirror, or randomly alter the Korean characters.
- Identity preservation: Use {원본 인물} as the reference for hairstyle silhouette, face impression, expression, outfit color family, and overall personality, while translating them into simplified {토이 스타일} toy proportions.
- Anatomy/layout invariants: Keep the toy proportions consistent and balanced, with a single centered character, proportional props, no extra limbs, no duplicate figures, and no distorted toy anatomy.
- Product realism: The display should feel physically photographed, with believable plastic, acrylic, printed-card texture, molded seams, small labels, contact shadows, and realistic scale relationships.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized celebrity likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Personal travel postcard poster with one traveler as the hero portrait, designed as a vertical vintage souvenir print.
Create a rich, realistic editorial-style travel keepsake that feels like a scanned postcard poster collected during a memorable trip, suitable for personal display, social posting, or print-like digital archiving.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: {원본 인물} is centered as the main hero, occupying about 40% of the frame height; the face sits in the upper-middle zone and the shoulders taper naturally into the lower-middle, integrated with the poster as if printed on textured postcard paper.
- Background treatment: Build the full-frame scenic backdrop from {여행지 무드}, using a believable coastal travel atmosphere with pale sky gradients, sunlit haze, distant shoreline shapes, sea-sand tones, a few small natural travel details, and gentle environmental depth.
- Framing and spacing: {프레임} wraps all four sides as a tactile postcard border with layered paper edges, thin inner rules, airmail strip accents, small corner registration marks, and a realistic printed shadow.
- Text hierarchy: Reserve the top 15% for {메인 문구} as the dominant headline, then add smaller postcard-style travel labels, date stamps, and caption text around the lower and side areas without competing with the title.
- Poster realism: Include a small postage-stamp illustration, circular postmark, postcard number, date/location label, handwritten-style caption, and tiny credit line to make the design feel like an actual souvenir print rather than a plain portrait mockup.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Central Portrait Layer: Place {원본 인물} cleanly at the center as a realistic travel-photo hero portrait, preserving natural facial proportions, realistic skin texture, crisp eye detail, and believable edge integration with the printed poster surface.
2. Scenic Background Layer: Fill the canvas with {여행지 무드}, rendered as soft coastal scenery with blurred horizon, airy sky color, warm reflected light, small beachside or travel-route details, and gentle distance haze that supports the traveler’s story.
3. Title Header Zone (top 15%): Set {메인 문구} across the upper area in large bold Korean type, centered, with generous tracking and strong poster presence so it reads instantly from afar.
4. Postcard Frame Layer: Surround the full composition with {프레임}, including thin border lines, a small stamp-icon accent, mail-card structure, airmail-style diagonal color marks, a circular postmark, and subtle paper layering that clearly signals vintage postcard design.
5. Travel Detail Layer: Add realistic printed micro-elements: “POSTCARD NO.1204”, “2026.05”, “여행의 기록”, “오늘의 바람”, “느리게 걷기”, “보통의 하루가 엽서가 되는 순간”, a small route-line graphic, tiny coordinate-like numbers, and a model/photo credit reading “MODEL · 나의 여행자”.
6. Bottom Caption Band: In the lower area, include a compact souvenir caption block with Korean text such as “좋은 날의 표정”, “다시 꺼내 보는 장면”, and “FROM THE COAST”, balanced with a small barcode-like postcard inventory mark and a short handwritten note.
7. Finish Details: Add subtle travel-print texture, light film grain, faint halftone speckles, mild paper fiber, slightly uneven ink density, and a soft vignette so the result feels like a real scanned souvenir poster rather than a flat digital advertisement.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Pretendard Bold for the main title at about 60pt, with clean Korean letterforms and strong stroke clarity; use smaller Pretendard Medium, serif travel-label type, and a light handwritten script for secondary postcard annotations.
- Color palette: Base the poster on {색감}; emphasize #DCEEFF soft blue, #F7E7A1 warm yellow, #FFF6EA cream, and muted sea-sand beige, with slightly lifted highlights and warm printed-paper undertones.
- Border/shadow: Apply a subtle drop shadow to the frame with 3px y-offset, 8px blur, and 20% opacity; keep the shadow soft and postcard-like, with slight edge depth as if the card is photographed or scanned.
- Surface texture: Use mild paper grain, slight print aging, gentle offset-print texture, tiny ink misregistration, and subtle halftone dots; maintain clean skin tones and an inviting travel-poster finish.
- Graphic accents: Add realistic souvenir graphics such as a small stamp block, postmark ring, ticket-stub divider, route line, tiny star/sea-breeze icons, and small caption rules that match the vintage postcard theme.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm film-camera look, like a Canon AE-1 with a 50mm f/1.8 lens, giving natural perspective and gentle depth separation.
- Lighting: Soft even daylight under a clear midday sky, with gentle highlights on the subject's face and a lightly brightened background to preserve the fresh travel-postcard feeling.
- Color grade: Bright airy film grade with pastel coastal blues, sunlit cream, and warm postcard warmth; keep contrast moderate and blacks slightly lifted.
- Material realism: The final image should resemble a high-quality printed travel postcard poster with visible paper fibers, slight ink texture, believable compositing, and tactile souvenir ephemera.

[6. MOOD]
Vintage travel poster meets modern personal souvenir print — like a Kinfolk-inspired editorial postcard with a 35mm film holiday-memory aesthetic, enriched with real postcard details, handwritten travel captions, soft coastal nostalgia, and a collectible keepsake feeling.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: “{메인 문구}” must appear exactly as written, with clean readable Korean characters and no broken glyphs.
- Render added Korean text clearly where used: “여행의 기록”, “오늘의 바람”, “느리게 걷기”, “보통의 하루가 엽서가 되는 순간”, “좋은 날의 표정”, “다시 꺼내 보는 장면”, and “MODEL · 나의 여행자”.
- Portrait integrity: {원본 인물} must keep natural facial features, correct proportions, realistic skin tones, and anatomically normal visible body parts; no facial warping, no extra limbs, and no distorted hands if visible.
- Layout invariant: The title must stay in the top 15% area, and the postcard frame must remain visible on all sides.
- Keep all postcard elements secondary to the hero portrait and main Korean title while making the composition feel like a real printed travel souvenir.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals, government marks, or certification badges
- Broken Korean characters or misspelled Korean text
- Real celebrity composites or unauthorized celebrity likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Indie album cover artwork in portrait format for digital music platforms, streaming thumbnails, vertical poster crops, and release announcement graphics.
Cinematic portrait-driven cover with realistic music-release details, tactile editorial texture, strong title hierarchy, and a premium indie-label feel.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: {원본 인물} centered and occupying about 70% of the vertical frame, with the face in the upper-middle third and the upper torso clearly readable.
- Background treatment: atmospheric studio-to-location hybrid backdrop in {색감}, transitioning from deep blue shadow zones into warm sunset tones, with subtle film grain, faint wall texture, soft haze, and natural bokeh-like light falloff.
- Text spacing: {앨범 제목} positioned near the top margin as the main cover title; {아티스트명} placed lower and smaller on the same center axis, creating a balanced poster-like hierarchy while leaving the face unobstructed.
- Additional album-cover details: add small realistic music-release typography such as “DIGITAL SINGLE”, “VOL. 01”, “2026.05 RELEASE”, “작사·작곡 {아티스트명}”, “감정의 밤을 지나”, a tiny catalog code like “IND-1203-KR”, and a small barcode/label-credit block near the lower edge.
- Framing direction: portrait crop with a slightly intimate close-up feel, preserving facial contours and avoiding wide-angle distortion.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero portrait layer (middle 70%): {원본 인물} rendered as the primary focal point, centered, crisp, and emotionally restrained, with the face clearly defined and the silhouette kept natural.
2. Background layer (full frame): a cinematic gradient wash in {색감}, softly blending from deep navy into amber-tinted dusk tones, enriched with subtle analog grain, faint paper-scanned texture, gentle lens bloom, and soft environmental shadow cues.
3. Title layer (top 15%): "{앨범 제목}" set above the subject in a bold, clean sans-serif treatment, highly legible against the background, with stable center alignment and a refined album-cover presence.
4. Artist layer (bottom 10%): "{아티스트명}" placed below the portrait area in smaller type, understated but readable, echoing the title’s spacing and alignment without competing for attention.
5. Release information layer: place tiny secondary Korean and English text around the lower third or bottom margin, including “DIGITAL SINGLE”, “2026.05.01”, “서울의 밤에서 녹음”, “작사·작곡 {아티스트명}”, “MIXED IN ROOM 27”, and “IND-1203-KR”, set like real indie-label packaging credits.
6. Barcode / label block: add a small vertical barcode area or compact rectangular metadata block near the lower-right edge, with micro text such as “Ⓟ 2026”, “All tracks by {아티스트명}”, and “KOREA INDIE RELEASE”; keep it secondary but believable.
7. Overall balance: maintain a clean editorial cover structure with the portrait as the emotional anchor, typography as the framing device, and realistic release details adding authenticity.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard Bold for {앨범 제목} at roughly 48–72px scale, Pretendard Regular for {아티스트명} at roughly 22–32px scale, both with clean kerning, center alignment, and high legibility.
- Secondary typography: use Pretendard Medium / Regular at 8–16px scale for release credits, catalog number, barcode text, and small Korean caption lines; align them carefully to feel like real album packaging.
- Color palette: {색감}, deep navy #0B1D3A, midnight blue #13294B, muted charcoal #1E1E24, warm amber #F2A65A, and soft dusk orange #D98B4B.
- Graphic details: add subtle analog film grain, slight halation around warm highlights, faint paper texture, tiny registration-like micro marks, and restrained label-credit blocks that support the indie album identity.
- Text separation: apply a subtle text-only soft drop shadow with 4px vertical offset, 12px blur, and 15% opacity for separation from the background.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 50mm portrait lens, f/2.8, shallow depth of field, high-resolution skin detail preserved without over-smoothing, framed like a premium music press portrait.
- Lighting: soft diffused key light from camera-left at about 45°, with a faint warm rim light from the right to echo sunset tones; gentle shadow falloff across the face.
- Color grade: deep blue shadows, warm orange-amber highlights, slightly desaturated mids, filmlike contrast, and a quiet midnight-cinema palette reminiscent of premium art-house poster grading.
- Realism treatment: preserve natural skin texture, realistic fabric detail, subtle catchlights in the eyes, believable background depth, and a printed-album-cover finish with slight grain and tonal softness.

[6. MOOD]
Cinematic indie album cover in a {무드} mood — like a quiet art-house film still released as a personal late-night single, intimate, atmospheric, and emotionally restrained.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: "{앨범 제목}", "{아티스트명}" must appear exactly as written, with no broken characters, spacing changes, or spelling changes.
- Additional Korean micro text should be readable and natural, such as “디지털 싱글”, “서울의 밤에서 녹음”, “작사·작곡 {아티스트명}”, and “감정의 밤을 지나”.
- Reference image integrity: {원본 인물} must remain a real person or authorized portrait source, with facial features kept natural and undistorted.
- Layout invariant: the portrait remains the dominant visual element, and both title and artist text stay clearly separated from the face.
- Album-cover authenticity: include believable release metadata, catalog code, barcode/label area, and small credits without overpowering the main portrait.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals or certification marks
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Virtual news anchor portrait for digital media, designed as a polished vertical broadcast poster.
Create a realistic medium-shot newsroom visual that reads like a prime-time TV news still, with a credible live-broadcast interface, layered studio graphics, and clear lower-third messaging.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: {원본 인물} centered and occupying the middle 60% of the frame, upper body only, facing camera with a calm anchor-like expression, wearing {의상}.
- Background treatment: Realistic {배경} interpreted as a contemporary broadcast newsroom with a subtle blue gradient, glass-panel reflections, LED wall graphics, distant newsroom monitors, soft studio depth, and faint geometric panel lines.
- Spacing and framing: Maintain a straight-on, stable broadcast framing with enough bottom space for the lower-third and ticker graphics; keep the subject dominant while allowing authentic newsroom details to support the scene.
- Broadcast details: Add a small top-left LIVE indicator, a top-right time/date bug, a side information panel with short Korean headlines, and a sleek anchor desk edge or glossy reflection at the bottom for realism.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero area (top 60%): {원본 인물} shown as the anchor figure, shoulders squared, crisp facial detail, natural skin texture, tidy hair silhouette, and {의상} clearly visible with realistic fabric folds, lapel seams, subtle highlights, and studio-light reflections.
2. Studio backdrop (middle 25%): {배경} rendered as a layered virtual newsroom set in navy and broadcast-blue tones, including blurred control-room screens, a panoramic LED world-map graphic, glass partitions, vertical light strips, and subtle reflections that create real studio depth.
3. Lower-third zone (bottom 15%): A professional news bar spanning most of the width, with "{프로그램명}" as the main title and "{자막}" as the subtitle, aligned left in a controlled broadcast layout with sharp edges, a thin white divider, blue gradient blocks, and a small red LIVE tag.
4. Ticker and metadata strip: Add a slim scrolling ticker below the main lower-third with short Korean broadcast text such as "주요 뉴스", "현장 연결", "날씨", "경제", plus a small date/time label like "2026.05.01 20:45" and a tiny page-style marker "NEWS DESK 01".
5. Side graphic module: Place a semi-transparent right-side panel behind the subject shoulder area with 2–3 compact headline bullets in Korean, for example "오늘의 이슈", "심층 분석", "전문가 인터뷰", using small but legible broadcast typography.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Pretendard Bold for "{프로그램명}" at about 18–22pt, and Pretendard Regular for "{자막}" at about 13–15pt; keep tracking tight, broadcast-clean, and highly legible.
- Additional text hierarchy: Use Pretendard SemiBold for the LIVE label, ticker category words, side headline bullets, and date/time bug; use smaller Pretendard Regular for micro text such as "서울 스튜디오", "HD LIVE", and "NEWS DESK 01".
- Color palette: Navy (#001F3F), Deep broadcast blue (#123A63), Light blue (#ADD8E6), Pale icy blue (#DCEEFF), White (#FFFFFF), plus a restrained red accent (#E31B23) for LIVE and breaking-news emphasis.
- Border/shadow: Lower-third bar with a soft drop shadow, 3px y-offset, 10px blur, 20% opacity; thin white divider lines, subtle glassmorphism panels, fine grid overlays, and glossy reflection details for a studio-graphic finish.
- Graphic realism: Include realistic broadcast UI layers, faint scanline texture on distant LED screens, soft reflections on the desk edge, and clean on-air graphic alignment that feels produced by a real TV news graphics package.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Full-frame 50mm lens at f/2.8, straight-on portrait framing, natural perspective with clean facial proportions and broadcast-friendly realism.
- Lighting: Soft studio key light from front-left at about 45°, gentle fill from front-right, subtle hair light to separate the subject from the blue background, no harsh contrast.
- Color grade: Neutral broadcast grade with a slight cool tint, clean whites, controlled blues, and mild contrast reduction for an on-air newsroom feel.
- Rendering quality: Photorealistic skin, realistic eye catchlights, crisp garment texture, controlled facial shadows, accurate depth of field on background monitors, and high-resolution broadcast-poster finish.

[6. MOOD]
Professional network news broadcast — polished prime-time anchor aesthetic, like a major TV newsroom still with credible live graphics, calm authority, and restrained editorial realism.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: "{프로그램명}" and "{자막}" must appear exactly as written in Korean with no broken characters.
- Render added Korean broadcast text clearly where used: "LIVE", "서울 스튜디오", "주요 뉴스", "현장 연결", "날씨", "경제", "오늘의 이슈", "심층 분석", "전문가 인터뷰", and "2026.05.01 20:45".
- Anatomy/layout invariants: Preserve natural proportions of {원본 인물}, keep the face undistorted, and maintain a realistic upper-body anchor pose.
- Identity preservation: Use {원본 인물} as the same person, retaining recognizable facial features while adapting lighting, posture, and wardrobe presentation to the newsroom setting.
- Broadcast composition: The lower-third must remain readable, horizontally aligned, and visually separated from the portrait; do not let text cover the subject’s eyes, nose, or mouth.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals or certification marks
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: top header occupies 18% of the frame, central palette grid 42%, usage note box 12%, and bottom mockup panel 28%.
- Background treatment: warm off-white paper texture #FAF8F4 with visible fine paper fibers, subtle warm-gray grain, faint print-registration specks, and matte editorial stock.

   - Card 1: show a large swatch block using {컬러 1} at the top of the card, then stack the hex code and descriptive label beneath in a tidy left-aligned hierarchy; add a tiny use tag such as LOGO / HEADER.
   - Card 2: show a large swatch block using {컬러 2} with the same hierarchy, spacing, and label placement as Card 1; add a tiny use tag such as POINT / BUTTON.
   - Card 3: show a large swatch block using {컬러 3}, with clear labels beneath and slightly darker text for legibility; add a tiny use tag such as BG / CARD.
   - Card 4: show a large swatch block using {컬러 4}, matching the other three cards exactly in proportions, label order, and spacing; add a tiny use tag such as WARM / BASE.
   - Add small measurement-style ticks and thin divider rules between cards, like a printed brand guideline sheet.
3. Middle area (12%):
   - Place {추천 사용처} inside a thin rounded gray information box spanning most of the width, centered horizontally with comfortable padding and a practical note-card feel.
   - Add a small label at the upper-left of the box: 추천 사용처, plus a tiny bookmark icon at the upper-right.
   - Include a secondary line in Korean below the main usage text: 톤 조합 비율 {비율} · 메인/포인트/배경 컬러로 분리해 사용.

   - Place small Korean sample copy near the previews: 신메뉴 안내, 톤앤무드 저장, 패키지 라벨.
   - Place a CTA button labeled {CTA} near the lower edge, followed by a tiny arrow →, using a filled pill shape and centered alignment.
   - Add a footer row with tiny social-card details: 공유 · 저장 · 팔레트 문의, a page indicator 01 / 05, and @brand.palette.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard + Noto Sans KR mix; title in Pretendard Bold 52px, eyebrow in Pretendard Medium 20px, supporting text in Noto Sans KR Regular 18px, hex labels in Pretendard SemiBold 16px.
- Color palette: exact swatches from {컬러 1}, {컬러 2}, {컬러 3}, {컬러 4}; supporting neutrals in #111111, #4A4A4A, #8C8C8C, background #FAF8F4.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px neutral borders on cards, soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 12% opacity on main panels, with subtle paper layering and printed divider lines.
- Layout details: use realistic editorial ornaments such as tiny arrows, section labels, page marks, dot separators, icon-sized bookmark/share symbols, and small caption strips.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]

- Lighting: even studio lighting from above with very soft fill from both sides, gentle paper shadows between layered cards, no harsh highlights, no color cast distortion.
- Color grade: true-to-source palette with neutral white balance, slightly soft editorial contrast, clean modern brand-board finish.
- Material realism: matte paper surface, fine ink edges, subtle fiber texture, slight shadow under raised panels, and crisp printed Korean typography.

[6. MOOD]

[7. CRITICAL]

[1. PURPOSE]

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]

- Spacing and framing: structured margins with layered card panels, soft dividers, small corner labels, date stamp, proposal ID, metric chips, and bottom CTA button anchored above the lower edge.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header area (top 18%): center-align {상단 문구} in medium-weight text above a larger bold {문서 제목}, with strong hierarchy and compact line spacing. Add a small upper-left document label reading 'CREATOR COLLAB PROPOSAL', an upper-right date stamp reading '2026.05 업데이트', and a tiny proposal code 'NO.1200 / VOL.05' in soft taupe.
2. Profile area (center-left 35%): place {크리에이터 사진} inside a perfect round frame with a thin gold ring, centered vertically in the midsection, clean cutout, soft realistic shadow, and a warm ivory inner backing. Add two small overlapping peach/gold badge stickers near the portrait edge reading 'BRAND FIT 92' and 'REELS READY'.
3. Creator identity lines (upper center-right): place {크리에이터 이름} as the primary line and {채널·팔로워} directly beneath it, aligned left with consistent line spacing and stronger weight for the name. Add a tiny handle label '@noeul_creator' and a small pill badge '협업 가능' near the identity area.
4. Proposal info stack (mid-right): render three neatly separated labeled rows for {블록 1}, {블록 2}, {블록 3}, each on its own line block with a subtle label-style emphasis, thin taupe dividers, and supporting micro text flow for quick scanning. Add small icons or bullet glyphs for concept, deliverables, and schedule, plus a tiny note line '검토 후 24시간 내 회신' below the stack.
5. Mini analytics strip (lower midsection): add three compact stat cards across the width above the CTA, reading '평균 조회율 18.6%', '저장률 7.4%', '여성 25-34 48%'. Use peach fills, charcoal text, and fine gold separators to make the proposal feel like a real creator media kit.
6. Bottom CTA area (bottom 12%): display a rounded peach button with the exact text '제안 및 문의하기' in white, centered horizontally and visually prominent. Add small contact microcopy beneath or beside it: 'contact@creator.kr · 카카오 채널 문의 가능', plus tiny share/save-style micro icons as decorative UI details.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard Bold for {문서 제목}, Pretendard SemiBold for {상단 문구}, badges, stat labels, and button text, Pretendard Regular for supporting lines; title about 34–40px feel, body 20–24px feel, button 22–24px feel, micro labels 10–14px feel.
- Color palette: Peach #FFCBA4, White #FFFFFF, Charcoal #36454F, Warm Ivory #FFF8F1, Gold #D8B46A, Soft Taupe #B9A89A.
- Border/shadow: thin gold ring around the profile frame, layered cream panels with realistic soft shadows, button with subtle 4px y-offset shadow, 12px blur, 15% opacity, stat cards with fine 1px taupe lines, small gold corner accents.
- Graphic details: include tasteful editorial stickers, dotted guide marks, document tabs, tiny check icons, page-code text, and paper texture while keeping all Korean text crisp and readable.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 with 85mm f/1.4 portrait look for the profile image crop, with shallow depth-of-field feel and clean facial centering.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left, gentle fill from right, even skin tones, realistic paper shadows, legible graphic layout, and subtle highlights on the gold ring and badges.
- Color grade: warm cream + peach + charcoal with restrained gold accents, slight editorial matte finish, realistic printed-card texture, tactile premium stationery feeling.

[6. MOOD]
Premium creator outreach card — Notion-style startup deck meets Kinfolk editorial layout, upgraded with authentic media-kit analytics, collaboration badges, and polished proposal-document details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: '함께 만드는 브랜드 콘텐츠', '협업 제안서', '@noeul_creator', '인스타 12.4K · 유튜브 8.2K', '콘셉트 — 데일리 라이프 + 카페 리뷰', '제공 내용 — 인스타 피드 1 + 릴스 1 + 스토리 3', '일정 — 5월 둘째 주 (5/13~5/19)', '제안 및 문의하기'.
- Additional Korean micro text must remain readable: '협업 가능', '평균 조회율 18.6%', '저장률 7.4%', '여성 25-34 48%', '검토 후 24시간 내 회신', '2026.05 업데이트'.
- Profile photo processing: center-cropped into a perfect circle, background softly blurred or replaced with a warm editorial fill, face and shoulders naturally framed, realistic skin tone and portrait proportions.
- Layout invariant: profile portrait stays on the left side and the three info blocks stay on the right side in a clear vertical stack.
- Preserve every placeholder exactly: {상단 문구}, {문서 제목}, {크리에이터 사진}, {크리에이터 이름}, {채널·팔로워}, {블록 1}, {블록 2}, {블록 3}.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall layout: Portrait 2:3 comparison card with a strong editorial top header, a balanced side-by-side comparison center, three compact improvement chips near the bottom, and subtle card-news footer details.
- Subject placement: Header occupies the top 15%, comparison panels fill the middle 68–70%, improvement chips sit in the lower 12–14%, and a slim footer/page indicator area sits at the very bottom without disturbing the three-chip structure.

- Framing direction: Keep both comparison photos locked to equal size, equal crop ratio, and equal vertical alignment so the visual change is easy to scan at a glance. Let the photos feel like real magazine cutouts with natural detail, believable lighting, and consistent scale.

Header area (top 15%): Place a small lime pill label reading "비교 리포트" at the upper left, a small issue/date label such as "VOL.1198 · 2026.05" at the upper right, then place {상단 문구} centered near the top in a bold, high-contrast line, with {제목} directly below it as the main title and a slightly larger visual weight. Add a thin decorative underline or lime highlight bar behind part of the title for a richer editorial card-news feel.
2. Comparison area (mid 68–70%):
   - Left panel: Place {비교 전 사진} in a rectangular photo frame on the left half, with a clear "BEFORE" label overlayed near the lower edge and a small Korean caption "변화 전" beneath or beside the label.
   - Right panel: Place {비교 후 사진} in a matching rectangular photo frame on the right half, with a clear "AFTER" label overlayed near the lower edge and a small Korean caption "변화 후" beneath or beside the label.
   - Alignment rule: Both panels must be identical in width, height, crop ratio, and baseline alignment for a precise side-by-side comparison.
   - Divider: Add a thin vertical divider or narrow lime-accent gap between the two panels, including a small circular center marker reading "VS" to make the comparison feel intentional and editorial.
